add.title: Playing dress-up: Four cross-dressers jailed in Oman — Roya News
add.summary: Roya News (19 Sep 2018), on the Public Prosecution's announcement: a Salalah preliminary court sentenced two men to four years in jail and fined them OMR 3,000 each for cross-dressing and sharing photos of themselves in women's clothes on social media, and two further men to three years with the same fine for featuring in the video; the sentences fall under the July 2018 Omani Penal Code provision (Article 22), under which 'any male that appears in female clothing or demeanor' may be fined up to OMR 3,000 and jailed up to one year, with additional 'publishing immoral acts on social media' charges. The article notes these follow January 2018 arrests by the Royal Oman Police of a group of men for dressing as women after social-media photos circulated. It documents court-ordered imprisonment of gender-nonconforming people in Oman, but contains no information on where inside the prison system those convicted were housed.
